scope: Reviewed the Japanese article and all twelve translations for the basic semiconductor explanation, historical attribution, Nobel wording, dates, and video/source links.
findings: Removed an unsupported generalization about how the researchers were initially evaluated in Japan.
Explained why blue LEDs required a wider-band-gap semiconductor and why GaN crystal growth and p-type conductivity were difficult.

Clarified that “nearly impossible” is rhetorical, not literal, and that the three researchers received the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics for efficient blue LEDs enabling bright, energy-saving white light sources.
Removed duplicate future dates, preserved original publication date, set lastmod, and added the official Nobel source in all locales.
